title: Malformed nested tool-call JSON causing structured-output parse failures in production
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) have escalated production failures where function/tool call responses containing nested JSON blobs repeatedly trigger structured-output parsing errors. Symptoms include: apps receiving JSONDecodeError or truncated structured payloads, downstream errors in customer microservices, and automated rollbacks on canary routes. The failures are intermittent but reproducible with certain nested quoting/escaping patterns and when KV cache hits return an older tool schema variant.

Observed across deployment modes: Hosted (most reports), Dedicated pools (2 customers with reserved capacity), and 1 Private on-prem customer with custom function schemas.

Hypothesis / Root cause:
- The structured-output parser uses a permissive heuristic to extract JSON from model text output (attempts to strip markdown fences and unescape). When the model emits nested JSON with backslashes and mixed quoting (e.g., nested triple-quoted strings, escaped newlines), our unescape logic double-unescapes sequences in edge cases, producing invalid JSON.
- KV cache + schema hashing: For cached function metadata we canonicalize the function schema before validating output. A difference in newline normalization (CRLF vs LF) between the canonicalizer in runtime-1.17 and the newer runtime-1.19 caused a schema-hash mismatch for some clients on Dedicated/Private that had older cached entries. In those cases, fallback code attempted a different parser path and hit the double-unescape bug.

Impact:
- High: customer-facing errors, production incidents, loss of automation for customers relying on structured tool responses (bills of materials, code generation, data extraction).

Repro steps (minimal):
1. Model configured to call tool `extract_items` with schema that expects a `details` field containing nested JSON string.
2. Provide prompt that encourages the model to emit JSON inside a string field with escaped quotes and newlines.
3. Send requests repeatedly to exercise cache hits (repeat same request to hit KV/cache route).
4. Observe JSONDecodeError in SDK structured output deserializer or truncated `details` content.

Immediate mitigation (short-term):
- Add an outbound gateway validation layer that checks tool-call outputs for balanced braces and rejects obviously corrupted payloads with a controlled error (allows graceful fallback to plain text response instead of raising). Rollout to Hosted within 24h.
- For Dedicated: provide configuration flag to bypass cached schema hash canonicalization to avoid mismatched parser paths (customer opt-in).
- For Private: ship advisory with suggested KVs to invalidate and recommended config to normalize line endings in custom schemas.

Proposed permanent fixes (medium-term):
1) Replace naive unescape-with-regex approach in structured-output parser with a deterministic balanced-brace JSON extractor that:
   - Finds the outermost JSON object/array using stack-based parsing tolerant to surrounding markdown fences,
   - Only performs a single canonical unescape pass with explicit rules for "\n" and "\" sequences,
   - Validates UTF-8 and rejects control characters that would make JSON invalid.
2) Standardize schema canonicalization across runtimes by introducing a stable serializer that normalizes line endings, key ordering (where safe), and whitespace before hashing.
3) Add unit + fuzz tests for nested quoting patterns and CRLF/LF variants.
4) Add telemetry: histogram of parser errors by failure type, and tag by deployment mode and schema-hash mismatch to surface regressions earlier.

Rollout plan: 
- Hotfix (gateway validation) to Hosted: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 24h if no regressions. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2541
- Dedicated: hot configuration flag and opt-in patch release to affected customers (ENG-incident playbook step).
- Permanent parser + canonicalizer change targeted for runtime-1.19 with feature flag; run canaries on non-critical routes for 7 days then full rollout. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2563 (parser rewrite), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2568 (canonicalizer).

Monitoring / Validation: 
- Dashboard: Structured parser failures panel (errors/min, broken down by error kind) https://dash.redwood.ai/d/r/structured-parsing
- Create synthetic probe set of 40 prompt+schema combos that exercise nested escaping; run every 5m across regions.

Notes / trade-offs: 
- Parser rewrite increases CPU per-request slightly due to stack-based extraction; we will benchmark and add a conditional fast-path for simple responses.
- Canonicalization/ordering of keys might cause false mismatches for intentionally unordered schema definitions; we will limit canonical ordering to stable, semantic fields and include a migration note.

Customer communication:
- Hosted: status page incident created and customers notified via support with link to advisory and workaround.
- Dedicated/Private: SE outreach in parallel; provide manual KV invalidation commands and optional patch.

Next steps / owners: 
- Liam O'Connor: lead the gateway validation hotfix and coordinate Hosted rollout (ETA 24h).
- Mei Chen: implement parser rewrite and unit/fuzz tests (ETA 2 weeks).
- Diego Ramirez: implement canonical schema serializer and add hash compatibility tests (ETA 1 week).
- Jordan Patel (Support): craft customer advisory and runbook.

Deliverables: 
- PR #2541 (gateway hotfix), PR #2563 (parser), PR #2568 (canonicalizer), runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFER/ENG-12845+Runbook

Construct prompt that asks for a JSON string with escaped quotes and newlines inside the 'details' field
Send the same request repeatedly to exercise KV cache hits
Observe structured-output deserializer throwing JSONDecodeError or returning truncated 'details'
